narrative: Segment map — Approach: In the half-flooded gatehouse, the keeper finds their wounded rival braced against a rusted sluice wheel while pursuit boots hammer across the iron bridge above. Cold water rises through the floor grating; each turn of the wheel exposes its operator to the bridge’s arrow slits. The keeper wants the rival’s cipher key and says, with restrained irony, “An inconvenient time to renegotiate.” The rival refuses to surrender it, reminding the keeper that their last bargain ended with a patrol walking into an ambush. Pressure: The keeper offers safe passage in exchange for the key, making terms instead of answering the accusation. When the rival calls the offer worthless, the keeper produces the one-use smoke charge kept for their own escape and wedges it beneath the bridge gears. The rival sees what its loss will cost but still holds back the key. Reversal: The pursuit reaches the gate. The rival can escape only if the sluice is opened, yet turning the wheel will leave the keeper in the line of fire. The keeper orders, “Three turns. Then you owe me the key and the luxury of doubting me somewhere dry.” They ignite the charge, remain at the wheel, and take a bolt through the sleeve while the rival crawls beneath the rising gate. Costly choice: Instead of following before the gears seize, the keeper completes the third turn, ruining the smoke charge and surrendering the safer route so the rival clears the channel. Observable change: From cover, the rival could flee with the cipher key. They return, cut the keeper’s pinned sleeve free, and press the key into their palm—but keep hold of the chain. “You carry it. I choose the road.” Outcome: They leave together by the drainage ledge, cooperation bounded by divided control. The keeper never asks forgiveness; their bargain has paid its price. Behind them, the jammed wheel shudders under pursuit, and the rival’s hand remains on the chain between them.
title: Terms at the Floodgate
